Title: Document H
Content: Source: Edward Livingston, member of the House of Representatives from New York, addressing Congress, `text(June 1798)`.

By [the Alien Act] the President alone is empowered to make the law; to fix in his own mind what acts, what words, what thoughts, or looks, shall constitute the crime contemplated by the bill; that is, the crime of being “suspected to be dangerous to the peace and safety of the United States.” This comes completely within the definition of despotism—a union of legislative, executive, and judicial powers.
